values.note: $20 a night, with the fee and registration procedure posted at the campground kiosk. A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to every state forest campground.

fees.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/cccbridge ('Overnight fees ($20 for most sites) and registration procedures are posted at the information kiosk at each campground'; 'A Recreation Passport (park pass) is required for vehicle entry into all state park and forest campgrounds') + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (CCC Bridge State Forest Campground: nightly fee $20), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Drinking water from a hand-pump well. Carry-in river access. ORVs and snowmobiles may run between the campground and nearby trails.

facilities.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/cccbridge ('There are vault toilets.' 'Potable (drinking) water is available from a hand-pump well.') + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (boat ramp/carry-in column), read 2026-10-25

booking.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/cccbridge ('No reservations. Sites available on a first-come, first-served basis.' 'Camping is limited to a 15-day maximum stay.') + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table ('Reservable at MiDNRReservations.com': no), read 2026-10-25

values.note: 31 'tent and small trailer sites' under red pines (agency wording, no length limit posted); the campground is also reachable from the Manistee River for canoe/kayak camping. One camping unit and six people per site.

sites.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/cccbridge + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (CCC Bridge State Forest Campground: 31 campsites; 'One camping unit and six people are allowed per site'), read 2026-10-25

note: Rustic state forest campground under red pines on the Manistee River (National Wild and Scenic River), 22 mi SW of Grayling via M-72 and Sunset Trail Rd SE; popular for paddling, tubing and trout fishing. ORV country: the Kalkaska Route passes the entrance and the Grand Traverse Motorcycle Trails are 1 mile south, so expect trail traffic. --Claude
summary: DNR page + SF amenity table: 31 tent/small-trailer sites, $20 at the kiosk + Recreation Passport, no electric, vault toilets, hand-pump water, first-come only (confirmed), 15-day max (now on the entry). Season open all year (already manual, matches). Phone differs (flag). No closure notice. Note trimmed of field restatements and the '~$15-20' figure.
